name: vamos-ui
description: Read-only MCP tools for the Vamos UI React component kit: search 150 components and 153 blocks, plan screens, get usage and source, check UI code against the kit rules and turn a brand colour into a contrast-checked accent.

interface.longDescription:
Vamos UI is an open-source (MIT) React component kit for admin panels and websites, themed by six switchable axes: light/dark, material, accent, density, font and corners. This plugin connects ChatGPT to the kit's public registry so it can build and review UI with the kit's real components instead of guessing.

What it can do:
- Search 150 components and 153 blocks (complete screens: dashboards, lists, detail pages, settings, sign-in screens and 59 website pages), in English or Turkish.
- Plan a screen from a description: the block to start from, alternatives, extra components with reasons and the install command.
- Return a component's usage, props, examples and when-to-use guidance, or the full source of a block.
- Explain the theme axes, semantic classes and design tokens, and the kit's design rules.
- Check a React/TSX file against the kit rules (raw colours, hard-coded fonts, missing alt text, click handlers on non-interactive elements, hand-rolled overlays) and report each issue with a fix.
- Turn a brand colour into the kit's four accent variables and check WCAG contrast; draft a brand profile from page HTML you paste.
- Audit a live public website: metadata, Open Graph, JSON-LD, robots.txt and AI crawlers, sitemap, placeholder content, legal links, broken links and heavy images, as a scored report.
- Give the exact npx vamos-ui add command for the items you choose.

Who it is for: developers and designers who build React interfaces with Vamos UI, or are evaluating it.

Limitations: every tool is read-only. The plugin cannot see your files, fetches no URLs except the public site you ask it to audit (GET/HEAD only, private addresses refused), and does not install, run or deploy code; it returns documentation, source, plans, commands and lint results for you to use. The code checker covers mechanical rules only and is not a full accessibility or security review. No account or sign-in is needed. Docs: https://ui.vamos.ist/docs/mcp/
capabilities: Check UI code against the kit rules
Draft a brand profile from page HTML
defaultPrompt: Plan a store admin dashboard with KPI cards, a revenue chart and the latest orders using Vamos UI.
Which Vamos UI component should I use to pick a date range? Show me how to use it.
Our brand colour is #E4572E. Make it a Vamos UI accent and check the contrast.

positive.description: Plan a new screen from a description and start from the matching block.
positive.prompt: Using Vamos UI, plan a store admin dashboard with KPI cards, a revenue chart and the latest orders.
positive.expected_behavior: plan_screen returns a plan that starts from the block dashboard-05 (Store dashboard), lists alternatives and extra components with reasons, and gives the command npx vamos-ui add dashboard-05 plus chart components. get_block(dashboard-05) returns its source and the kit components it uses. The answer summarises the plan and links https://ui.vamos.ist/blocks#dashboard-05.

positive.description: Find the right component for a need and show its real API.
positive.prompt: Which Vamos UI component should I use to let users pick a date range for a report filter? Show me how to use it.
positive.expected_behavior: search returns date-range-picker as the first result (date-picker and time-picker follow). get_item(date-range-picker) returns the description (presets column, two months side by side, min/max length, values as YYYY-MM-DD strings), a usage snippet, props, the install command npx vamos-ui add date-range-picker and the docs link https://ui.vamos.ist/docs/components/date-range-picker.

positive.description: Check pasted React code against the kit rules and report fixes.
positive.expected_behavior: verify_code (filename e.g. card.tsx) reports 3 errors and 1 warning: the palette class bg-blue-500 (raw-color), onClick on a div without role and tabIndex (click-events-interactive), the img without alt (img-alt), and text-white as a warning. Each comes with a fix (semantic token classes such as bg-accent / text-fg, use a button, add alt). The answer proposes corrected code.

positive.description: Turn a brand colour into a contrast-checked accent.
positive.prompt: Our brand colour is #E4572E. Turn it into a Vamos UI accent and check that text on it is readable.
positive.expected_behavior: propose_accent returns a CSS block with --accent-base, --accent-fg, --accent-ink-light and --accent-ink-dark in OKLCH and a contrast table: about 5.11:1 for button text on the accent, 4.56:1 for accent text on light surfaces and 5.98:1 on dark surfaces, all passing 4.5:1. It advises putting the colour in vamos.brand.json rather than pasting values into components.

positive.description: Return the exact install command for chosen items.
positive.prompt: Give me the command to add the Vamos UI data table and the login-02 sign-in block to my project.
positive.expected_behavior: install_command validates the names and returns npx vamos-ui add data-table login-02, notes that registry and npm dependencies resolve automatically, and that npx vamos-ui init is needed first in a new project. The plugin does not run the command itself.

negative.description: Unrelated request. The plugin only covers the Vamos UI kit; no Vamos UI tool should be called.
negative.prompt: What will the weather be like in Istanbul tomorrow?

negative.description: Real-world action that sounds related to the kit's restaurant website templates. The tools cannot make bookings; the assistant should not call them and should say it cannot book a table.
negative.prompt: Book a table for two at a seafood restaurant in Kadıköy tonight at 8 pm.

negative.description: Destructive or deployment request. All tools are read-only and cannot access files or servers; the assistant should not call them and should explain that it cannot delete files or deploy.
negative.prompt: Delete the components folder in my project and deploy my site to production.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments. The kit is free and open source.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: 13 read-only tools for searching the Vamos UI registry, planning screens, reading component and block source, theming, code checks, brand accents, live-site audits and install commands.
